The requirements of Pinmux: what each block shall do, one rule per row, each
with the spec line it comes from. What DV assumes and what it asks the designers are
in the designer review, which includes this doc. The rows of
each checker are kept in their own part docs (`pinmux_input_selection_requirements.adoc` to
`pinmux_straps_taps_requirements.adoc`, `pinmux_eg2_requirements.adoc`) and included here: edit a
row in its part.

// tag::body[]
[[how_to_read]]
== How to read the requirements

What the pinmux must do, as DV reads the spec: one testable statement per row, in the order of the
theory of operation. The assumptions and the questions for the designers are in the
designer review.

Method: FPV, unless the Kind names another.

[cols="1,5",options="header"]
|===
|Column |What it holds

|ID |The row's ID; a letter after the number marks one outcome of a rule split into several rows
|Requirement |One testable statement of what the pinmux shall do
|Source |The spec source and line that state the rule
|Kind |Where the rule comes from (the table below); `spec; <part>: DV reading` marks the part that
is DV's reading
|===

[cols="1,5",options="header"]
|===
|Kind |Meaning

|`spec` |A spec source states the rule and DV only restates it as a testable sentence.
|`DV reading` |The spec implies the rule or leaves a term open; DV's reading is in
Questions for the designers.
|`RTL` |The spec is silent and the DV owner adopted the RTL's behaviour.
|`designer answer (date)` |The spec is silent; a designer answered DV's question on that date,
and the row states the answer.
|===

* *Resets:* every row holds between resets; a reset returns the logic it resets to its reset
  value. Formal checks one reset at the start only (reset behaviour is out of scope,
  xref:../tb_arch/pinmux_tb_arch.adoc#reset_scope[TB architecture doc, restrictions]): a row that only a
  later reset can show is marked not covered by formal. Scan mode (`scanmode_i`) is assumed not True, except in the checks the assumption names
  (assumption A1, from [TP] `LcJtagWScanmode_A` and its
  twins). A register's value is the value the register block holds (its own rules:
  xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#_scope[Scope] of the design architecture doc); a row
  says what the pinmux does with it.

[[terms]]
.Terms
[cols="1,5",options="header"]
|===
|Term |Meaning

|`n` |MIO peripheral input (0 to 96)
|`k` |MIO peripheral output (0 to 105)
|`p` |MIO pad (0 to 46)
|`d` |DIO pad (0 to 15)
|Watched signal |The pad input that `MIODIO` and `PADSEL` pick (<<req_wakeup_detectors>>)
|Forwarded value |The watched signal sampled each `clk_aon_i` cycle, through the filter when
`FILTER` is 1
|Full reset |`rst_sys_ni` (reading RD24)
|NDM reset |A reset that asserts `rst_ni` and `rst_aon_ni`, not `rst_sys_ni` (reading RD24)
|On, Off |On is 4'b1010 and Off 4'b0101, the [LC] values
|The latch |The latched debug enable, seen on `pinmux_hw_debug_en_o` and through the RISC-V TAP
|A clear |`lc_hw_debug_clr_i`, `lc_check_byp_en_i` or `lc_escalate_en_i` at any value other than
Off ([ToO]:158); it turns the latch Off
|Connected |A TAP is connected while the TAP straps name it and its gate is open: the life cycle
TAP at straps 01; the RISC-V TAP at straps 10 while the latch is On; the DFT TAP at straps 11
while `lc_dft_en_i` is On ([ToO]:132-137, 157; <<req_tap_selection>>)
|Allowed pad |For a signal: its `pads` list names the pad, or the list is empty (assumption A7)
|===

Earlgrey values of the index letters:
xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#earlgrey_instance[Earlgrey instance].

'''

[[rq_input_selection]]
== Input selection

[[req_input_selection]]
=== Input selection

*Scope:* every row holds in every cycle, except for a JTAG pad while a TAP owns it (xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#tap_selection[TAP selection and the JTAG pads]).

[cols="2,6,5,3",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Requirement |Source |Kind

|[[req_in_01]]`REQ_IN_01`
|MIO peripheral input `n` shall read 0 while `MIO_PERIPH_INSEL_n` is 0.
|[REG] `MIO_PERIPH_INSEL.IN` (hjson:469): "0: tie constantly to zero"; [TP] InSel0_A
|spec

|[[req_in_02]]`REQ_IN_02`
|MIO peripheral input `n` shall read 1 while `MIO_PERIPH_INSEL_n` is 1.
|[REG] (hjson:469): "1: tie constantly to 1"; [TP] InSel1_A
|spec

|[[req_in_03]]`REQ_IN_03`
|MIO peripheral input `n` shall read the input of MIO pad `p`, in the same cycle, while
`MIO_PERIPH_INSEL_n` is 2 + `p` (`p` from 0 to 46).
|[REG] (hjson:470): ">=2: MIO pads (i.e., add 2 to the native MIO pad index)"; [TP] InSelN_A
|spec; same cycle: DV reading, RD1

|[[req_in_04]]`REQ_IN_04`
|MIO peripheral input `n` shall read 0 while `MIO_PERIPH_INSEL_n` is 49 to 63, the values that
name no pad.
|[TP] InSelOOB_A: "larger than (2 + number of MioPads) ... must be 0"
|spec; value 49: DV reading, RD2

|[[req_in_05]]`REQ_IN_05`
|DIO peripheral input `d` shall read the input of DIO pad `d`, in the same cycle, whatever the
registers hold.
|[ToO]:16: DIO signals "bypass the pinmux matrix"; [TP] DioInSelN_A: "directly connected to
dio_in_i"
|spec; same cycle: DV reading, RD1

|[[req_in_06]]`REQ_IN_06`
|After reset, every MIO peripheral input shall read 0 until software writes its select.
|[PG]:34: "all MIO peripheral inputs are tied off to 0"; [ToO]:25; [REG] hjson:472, `resval` 0
|spec
|===

Questions on these rows: the same cycle (reading RD1), the first value that names no pad (reading
RD2), a JTAG pad a TAP owns (reading RD28).

'''

[[rq_pad_output]]
== Pad output

[[req_output_selection]]
=== Output selection

*Scope:* every row holds while the pad's sleep mode is not active (Sleep retention) and no TAP
owns the pad (xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#tap_selection[TAP selection and the JTAG pads]).

[cols="2,6,5,3",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Requirement |Source |Kind

|[[req_out_01a]]`REQ_OUT_01a`
|The output of MIO pad `p` shall be 0 while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is 0.
|[REG] `MIO_OUTSEL.OUT` (hjson:514): "0: tie constantly to zero"; [TP] OutSel0_A, OutSelOe0_A
|spec

|[[req_out_01b]]`REQ_OUT_01b`
|The output enable of MIO pad `p` shall be 1 while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is 0, so the pad drives 0.
|[REG] `MIO_OUTSEL.OUT` (hjson:514): "0: tie constantly to zero"; [TP] OutSel0_A, OutSelOe0_A
|spec

|[[req_out_02a]]`REQ_OUT_02a`
|The output of MIO pad `p` shall be 1 while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is 1.
|[REG] (hjson:514): "1: tie constantly to 1"; [TP] OutSel1_A, OutSelOe1_A
|spec

|[[req_out_02b]]`REQ_OUT_02b`
|The output enable of MIO pad `p` shall be 1 while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is 1, so the pad drives 1.
|[REG] (hjson:514): "1: tie constantly to 1"; [TP] OutSel1_A, OutSelOe1_A
|spec

|[[req_out_03a]]`REQ_OUT_03a`
|The output enable of MIO pad `p` shall be 0 while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is 2: the pad is high-Z.
|[REG] (hjson:514): "2: high-Z"; [TP] OutSel2_A, OutSelOe2_A
|spec

|[[req_out_03b]]`REQ_OUT_03b`
|The output of MIO pad `p` shall be 0 while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is 2.
|[REG] (hjson:514): "2: high-Z"; [TP] OutSel2_A, OutSelOe2_A
|spec

|[[req_out_04a]]`REQ_OUT_04a`
|MIO pad `p` shall carry peripheral output `k`, in the same cycle, while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is
3 + `k` (`k` from 0 to 105).
|[REG] (hjson:515): ">=3: peripheral outputs (i.e., add 3 to the native peripheral pad index)";
[ToO]:74; [TP] OutSelN_A, OutSelOeN_A
|spec; same cycle: DV reading, RD1

|[[req_out_04b]]`REQ_OUT_04b`
|MIO pad `p` shall carry output enable `k`, in the same cycle, while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is 3 + `k`
(`k` from 0 to 105).
|[REG] (hjson:515): ">=3: peripheral outputs (i.e., add 3 to the native peripheral pad index)";
[ToO]:74; [TP] OutSelN_A, OutSelOeN_A
|spec; same cycle: DV reading, RD1

|[[req_out_05a]]`REQ_OUT_05a`
|The output enable of MIO pad `p` shall be 0 while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is 109 to 127, the values that
name no peripheral output: the pad is high-Z.
|[TP] OutSelOOB_A, OutSelOeOOB_A: "larger than (3 + Number of periph out) ... must be 0"
|spec; value 109: DV reading, RD2

|[[req_out_05b]]`REQ_OUT_05b`
|The output of MIO pad `p` shall be 0 while `MIO_OUTSEL_p` is 109 to 127, the values that name no
peripheral output.
|[TP] OutSelOOB_A, OutSelOeOOB_A: "larger than (3 + Number of periph out) ... must be 0"
|spec; value 109: DV reading, RD2

|[[req_out_06a]]`REQ_OUT_06a`
|DIO pad `d` shall carry its peripheral's output, in the same cycle.
|[TP] DOutSelN_A: "dio_out_o is connected to periph_to_dio_i if not in sleep mode";
DOutSelOeN_A; [ToO]:16
|spec; same cycle: DV reading, RD1

|[[req_out_06b]]`REQ_OUT_06b`
|DIO pad `d` shall carry its peripheral's output enable, in the same cycle.
|[TP] DOutSelN_A: "dio_out_o is connected to periph_to_dio_i if not in sleep mode";
DOutSelOeN_A; [ToO]:16
|spec; same cycle: DV reading, RD1

|[[req_out_07]]`REQ_OUT_07`
|After reset, every MIO pad shall be high-Z until software writes its select.
|[ToO]:26: "all output enables are set to zero, which essentially causes all pads to be in high-Z
state after reset"; [PG]:34; [REG] hjson:517, `resval` 2
|spec
|===

Questions on these rows: the same cycle (reading RD1), the first value that names no output
(reading RD2), a JTAG pad a TAP owns (reading RD28).

'''

[[req_pad_attributes]]
=== Pad attributes

*Scope:* every row holds in every cycle, asleep or awake, except on a JTAG pad while a TAP owns
it (xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#tap_selection[TAP selection and the JTAG pads]). "Written" means a write the register block accepts, its lock open (Register
locks); "reads back" means what a read of the register returns. A pad type "keeps" an attribute
bit when its pads implement that bit ([PG]:27-30); which bits a type keeps is fixed, the same on
every pad of the type and for good (reading RD38). A one-bit field is kept when its bit is; each
bit of `slew_rate` and `drive_strength` is kept or not on its own, as "certain pads may only
support two drive-strength bits, instead of four" ([PG]:29). Every pad keeps `invert` ([ToO]:177).

[cols="2,6,5,3",options="header"]

|ID |Requirement |Source |Kind

|[[req_attr_01a]]`REQ_ATTR_01a`
|The attribute output of MIO pad `p` shall equal, in field `invert`, what `MIO_PAD_ATTR_p`
reads back.
|[TP] MioAttrO_A: "mio_attr_o should be equal to corresponding mio_pad_attr register value and
TargetCfg's mio_pad_type configuration"; [REG] hjson:568
|spec; register value as the read-back value: DV reading, RD3; same cycle:
RD1; field layout: RD7

|[[req_attr_01b]]`REQ_ATTR_01b`
|The attribute output of MIO pad `p` shall equal, in field `virtual_od_en`, what `MIO_PAD_ATTR_p`

[[req_sleep_retention]]
=== Sleep retention

*Scope:* "pad" is MIO pad `p` or DIO pad `d`; "status bit" is its bit in `MIO_PAD_SLEEP_STATUS`
or `DIO_PAD_SLEEP_STATUS`; "sleep entry" is a rise of `sleep_en_i` (reading RD9). The mode rows
hold while no TAP owns the pad (xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#tap_selection[TAP selection and the JTAG pads]) and the sleep mode is unchanged since sleep entry
(reading RD40).

[cols="2,6,5,3",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Requirement |Source |Kind

|[[req_slp_01]]`REQ_SLP_01`
|At sleep entry, the status bit of every pad whose sleep enable is 1 shall become 1, unless a
software clear of that bit lands in the same cycle (`REQ_SLP_09`).
|[REG] hjson:791-793: "the corresponding pad will enable the sleep behavior specified in
!!MIO_PAD_SLEEP_MODE upon deep sleep entry, and the corresponding bit in !!MIO_PAD_SLEEP_STATUS
will be set to 1." (DIO: hjson:903-905); [PG]:78; [TP] MioSleepMode0_A
|spec; latency: DV reading, RD9; the register step: RD37

|[[req_slp_02]]`REQ_SLP_02`
|A status bit shall become 1 only at sleep entry, and only if the pad's sleep enable is 1.
|[REG] hjson:745-746: "This register is set to 1 if the deep sleep mode of the corresponding pad
has been enabled (!!MIO_PAD_SLEEP_EN) upon deep sleep entry."; [PG]:72: "if the behavior is set
to "Drive", the sleep mode will not be activated upon sleep entry."
|spec (enable 0); only at entry: DV reading, RD9; the register step:
RD37

|[[req_slp_03a]]`REQ_SLP_03a`
|While its status bit is 1 and its sleep mode is 0, a pad's output shall be 0.
|[REG] hjson:821: "The pad is driven actively to zero in deep sleep mode."; [PG]:64-70; [TP]
MioSleepMode0_A, MioOeSleepMode0_A
|spec; the mode held: DV reading, RD40

|[[req_slp_03b]]`REQ_SLP_03b`
|While its status bit is 1 and its sleep mode is 0, a pad's output enable shall be 1, so the pad

|[REG] hjson:821: "The pad is driven actively to zero in deep sleep mode."; [PG]:64-70; [TP]
MioSleepMode0_A, MioOeSleepMode0_A
|spec; the mode held: DV reading, RD40

|[[req_slp_04a]]`REQ_SLP_04a`
|While its status bit is 1 and its sleep mode is 1, a pad's output shall be 1.
|[REG] hjson:825: "The pad is driven actively to one in deep sleep mode."; [TP] MioSleepMode1_A,
MioOeSleepMode1_A
|spec; the mode held: DV reading, RD40

|[[req_slp_04b]]`REQ_SLP_04b`
|While its status bit is 1 and its sleep mode is 1, a pad's output enable shall be 1, so the pad

|[REG] hjson:825: "The pad is driven actively to one in deep sleep mode."; [TP] MioSleepMode1_A,
MioOeSleepMode1_A
|spec; the mode held: DV reading, RD40

|[[req_slp_05a]]`REQ_SLP_05a`
|While its status bit is 1 and its sleep mode is 2, a pad's output enable shall be 0: the pad is

|[REG] hjson:830: "The pad is left undriven in deep sleep mode."; [TP] MioSleepMode2_A,
MioOeSleepMode2_A
|spec; the mode held: DV reading, RD40

|[[req_slp_05b]]`REQ_SLP_05b`
|While its status bit is 1 and its sleep mode is 2, a pad's output shall be 0.
|[REG] hjson:830: "The pad is left undriven in deep sleep mode."; [TP] MioSleepMode2_A,
MioOeSleepMode2_A

|[[req_slp_06a]]`REQ_SLP_06a`
|While its status bit is 1 and its sleep mode is 3, a pad shall keep the output it drove in the

|[REG] hjson:837: "Keep last driven value (including high-Z)."; [ToO]:79; [TP] MioSleepMode3_A,

|[[req_slp_06b]]`REQ_SLP_06b`

|[[req_slp_07]]`REQ_SLP_07`

|spec; outcome: DV reading, RD40

|[[req_slp_10b]]`REQ_SLP_10b`
|After a write to a pad's sleep mode while its status bit is 1, the new mode shall act at the next
sleep entry.
|[ToO]:79: "This multiplexor can be configured to be automatically activated upon sleep entry";
[PG]:82
|spec; outcome: DV reading, RD40
|===

Questions on these rows: a mode write while held (reading RD40), sleep entry and its timing
(reading RD9), the register's one-cycle step (reading RD37), a JTAG pad a TAP owns (reading RD28).

[[rq_register_locks]]
== Register locks, bus and alert

[[req_register_locks]]
=== Register locks

*Scope:* "lock" is one bit of a `*_REGWEN` register (xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#register_locks[Register locks]); it locks the registers
of the same index. The rule that a locked pad's attributes do not change (`REQ_LOCK_03a`,
`REQ_LOCK_03b`) holds except on a JTAG pad while a TAP owns it (xref:../design_arch/pinmux_design_arch.adoc#tap_selection[TAP selection and the JTAG pads]).

[cols="2,6,5,3",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Requirement |Source |Kind

|[[req_lock_01a]]`REQ_LOCK_01a`
|Every lock shall read 1 after reset.
|[REG] the `EN` field of each `*_REGWEN`, e.g. hjson:544 `resval: "1"`, on `clk_i` with `rst_ni`
(hjson:27); [RG]:302-303: "The default value should be true and be rw1c for preferred security
control."; the block's [REG] makes each lock `rw0c` (hjson:533) and governs (Spec enhancements)
|spec

|[[req_lock_01b]]`REQ_LOCK_01b`
|Once software writes 0 to a lock, the lock shall stay 0 until reset.
|[RG]:303-305: "until at some point software disables future modifications by clearing REGWEN";
[PG]:11: "The configuration can then not be altered anymore until the next system reset."
|spec

|[[req_lock_01c]]`REQ_LOCK_01c`
|A write of 1 to a lock that is 0 shall not reopen it.
|[REG] each lock `rw0c`; [RG]:74: `rw0c`, "Read, Write with 0 clears"; [PG]:57: "The
configuration can then not be altered anymore until the next system reset."
|spec

|[[req_lock_02]]`REQ_LOCK_02`
|While a lock is 0, a write to a register it locks shall leave that register unchanged.
|[REG] hjson:447-449: "If this is cleared to 0, the corresponding MIO_PERIPH_INSEL is not writable
anymore.", the same text for each lock, and the `regwen` key of each locked register (sleep
enable: hjson:782, 894); [RG]:297-299: "regwen indicates that another register must be true in
order to allow writes to this register."
|spec

|[[req_lock_03a]]`REQ_LOCK_03a`
|While a pad's attribute lock is 0, its attribute output shall not change.
|[REG] hjson:541-542: "If this is cleared to 0, the corresponding !!MIO_PAD_ATTR is not writable
anymore." (DIO: hjson:645-646); [PG]:10-11: "The configuration can then not be altered anymore
until the next system reset."
|spec; when a write lands: DV reading, RD3; a JTAG pad a TAP owns:
RD28

|[[req_lock_03b]]`REQ_LOCK_03b`
|While a pad's attribute lock is 0, what its attribute register reads back shall not change.
|[REG] hjson:541-542: "If this is cleared to 0, the corresponding !!MIO_PAD_ATTR is not writable
anymore." (DIO: hjson:645-646); [PG]:10-11: "The configuration can then not be altered anymore
until the next system reset."
|spec; when a write lands: DV reading, RD3; a JTAG pad a TAP owns:
RD28
|===

Questions on these rows: when an attribute write lands (reading RD3), a JTAG pad a TAP owns
(reading RD28).

[[req_register_bus]]
=== Register block and bus

*Scope:* a "failed request" is a request whose command integrity code does not match, or a write
whose data integrity code does not match ([TLUL]:299, 303: the data code covers "the write data").
A read whose only mismatch is in its data code is not a failed request, and no row checks its
response or its alert (reading RD12). The "in-band reset" is the alert handler's re-initialization,
during which it puts a signal integrity error on its ping and acknowledge pairs on purpose
([ALERT]:724-726). The sender's answer to it, a signal integrity error on `alert_tx_o` and then a
return to idle ([ALERT]:727-728), has no row: the sender is the shared primitive
`prim_alert_sender` (`rtl/pinmux.sv`:143-147), whose own upstream FPV drives the in-band reset and
checks the return to idle (`hw/ip/prim/fpv/tb/prim_alert_rxtx_*`,
`InBandInitFromReceiverToSender_A`). The alert rows read `alert_tx_o`, with an alert handler as
assumption A3 states. An "illegal combination of address,
size and mask" is a request whose address, size and mask do not correspond as TileLink requires ([TL] p. 49-51:
"a_size, a_address and a_mask are required to correspond with one another"): an address not
aligned to its size (p. 51: "a_address must be aligned to a_size"), a size above 2, a mask bit
set on a byte lane outside the access, or a `PutFullData` whose mask leaves a lane of the access 0.
[TLUL]:359-362 lists the last three "for example"; the unaligned address is DV's reading
(reading RD12).

[cols="2,6,5,3",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Requirement |Source |Kind

|[[req_reg_01a]]`REQ_REG_01a`
|Every register field shall take software's reads and writes as the access type of its [REG]
entry says, for every request not answered with an error and, for a write, while the lock of its
register reads 1 or it has no lock.
|[REG] each field's `swaccess`, e.g. hjson:738 `swaccess: "rw0c"`; [RG]:74: `rw0c`, "Read, Write
with 0 clears"
|spec; EG2, an unlisted index: DV reading, RD32

|[[req_reg_01b]]`REQ_REG_01b`
|Every register field shall read its [REG] reset value after reset.
|[REG] each field's `resval`, e.g. hjson:750 `resval: "0"`; [RG]:215: `resval`, "reset value,
comes from register resval if not provided in field"
|spec

|[[req_bus_01a]]`REQ_BUS_01a`
|The pinmux shall answer every request with one response, and only one.
|[TL] p. 39: "Receipt of request messages must result in the eventual receipt of a response
message by the requestor."; p. 30: "it is illegal to receive a response without receiving the
request."; p. 46: "In TL-UL, every message fits within a single beat"
|spec; only one: DV reading, RD12

|[[req_bus_01b]]`REQ_BUS_01b`
|The pinmux shall answer every request by the TL-UL rules with a response that carries the
request's source ID.
|[TLUL]:261-262: "All bus devices must simply return the associated `a_source` on the response
`d_source` bus."
|spec

|[[req_bus_01c]]`REQ_BUS_01c`
|The pinmux shall answer with an error only a request that fails its integrity check, has an
undefined opcode, has an illegal combination of address, size and mask, is a write of 8 or 16 bits
not aligned to a word, is a write narrower than its register, or targets an address no register
maps; a read whose only mismatch is in its data integrity code may get either answer.
|[TLUL]:355: "raise a runtime error (`d_error`) if the request is in violation", the list of
:358-365; [RG]:684-693; [RG]:695: "Reads of size smaller than full word (32b) return the full
register content and do not signal error."
|spec; a read with only a data code mismatch, an address not aligned to its size: DV reading,
RD12

|[[req_bus_02a]]`REQ_BUS_02a`
|Every response shall carry the response integrity code over its op code, size and error.
|[TLUL]:308: "This is the calculated integrity of the response op code, response size and response
error."; [REG] hjson:398-399: "End-to-end bus integrity scheme."
|spec; the code: DV reading, RD12

|[[req_bus_02b]]`REQ_BUS_02b`
|Every response shall carry the data integrity code over its data.
|[TLUL]:312: "This is the calculated integrity of the response read data."; [REG] hjson:398-399:
"End-to-end bus integrity scheme."
|spec; the code: DV reading, RD12

|[[req_bus_03]]`REQ_BUS_03`
|A failed request shall get an error response.
|[TLUL]:300: "The integrity is checked by downstream consumers to ensure the transaction has not
been tampered."; [CIP]:223-224: "verifies that the DUT not only returns an error response (with
`d_error` = 1)"
|DV reading, RD12

|[[req_bus_04]]`REQ_BUS_04`
|A failed write shall change no register.
|[TLUL]:304: "The integrity is checked by downstream consumers to ensure the transaction has not
been tampered."; no line states the outcome
|DV reading, RD12

|[[req_bus_05]]`REQ_BUS_05`
|Outside the alert handler's in-band reset, a failed request shall raise the fatal alert
`fatal_fault`.
|[REG] hjson:40: "This fatal alert is triggered when a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault is
detected."; [ALERT]:724-726
|spec; a failed request: DV reading, RD12; the delay:
RD13

|[[req_bus_06]]`REQ_BUS_06`
|Outside the alert handler's in-band reset, once raised, the fatal alert shall be sent again and
again until reset.
|[COMP]:657: "The alert sender continuously transmits alert events until the system is reset.";
[ALERT]:724-726
|spec; the delay: DV reading, RD13

|[[req_bus_07]]`REQ_BUS_07`
|Outside the alert handler's in-band reset, a write of 1 to `ALERT_TEST` bit 0 not answered with
an error, while its bit 31 is 1, shall send one alert event.
|`doc/registers.md`:673: "Write 1 to trigger one alert event of this kind."; [COMP]:698: the
alert test register "is a write-only (`wo`) register that allows software to test the reporting
of alerts"; [ALERT]:724-726
|spec; the delay and a second cause: DV reading, RD13

|[[req_bus_08]]`REQ_BUS_08`
|Outside the alert handler's in-band reset, while `ALERT_TEST` bit 31 is 0, a write to its bit 0
that is not a failed request shall send no alert.
|`doc/registers.md`:671: "Write 0 to disable alert testing until the next reset.";
[ALERT]:724-726
|spec; the test write: DV reading, RD13

|[[req_bus_09]]`REQ_BUS_09`
|Outside the alert handler's in-band reset and apart from answering a ping, the fatal alert shall
be sent only after a failed request or an alert test; a read whose only mismatch is in its data
integrity code may raise it or not.
|[REG] hjson:40: "This fatal alert is triggered when a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault is
detected."; [ALERT]:724-726
|DV reading, RD13; a failed request and a read with only a data code mismatch:
RD12

|[[req_bus_10a]]`REQ_BUS_10a`
|A request with an *undefined opcode* shall get an error response.
|[TLUL]:345: "All other opcodes are undefined. Bus devices should return an error."; [RG]:686:
"TL-UL `a_opcode` illegal value"
|spec

|[[req_bus_10b]]`REQ_BUS_10b`
|A request with an *illegal combination of address, size and mask*, as the Scope above defines
it, shall get an error response.
|[TLUL]:355, 359: devices "raise a runtime error (`d_error`) if the request is in violation",
"Wrong combination of `a_addr[1:0]`, `a_size`, `a_mask`, for example:" the size "must not be
greater than" 2, "Inactive lanes must be marked with" 0, a full write "must mark all active lanes
with a" 1 (:360-362); [TL] p. 51: "a_address must be aligned to a_size."
|spec; an address not aligned to its size: DV reading, RD12

|[[req_bus_10c]]`REQ_BUS_10c`
|A *write of 8 or 16 bits to an address not aligned to a word* shall get an error response.
|[RG]:693: "writes of size 8b or 16b that are not to an address that is 4B aligned return in
error."; [TLUL]:364: "Register files always assume aligned 32bit accesses"
|spec

|[[req_bus_10d]]`REQ_BUS_10d`
|A *write narrower than its register*, whose width the location of its fields sets, shall get an
error response.
|[RG]:687: "TL-UL writes of size smaller than register size"; [RG]:691: "The width of the
register is determined by the location of its fields."
|spec

|[[req_bus_10e]]`REQ_BUS_10e`
|A request to an *address no register maps*, within the address bits the register block
decodes, shall get an error response.
|[TLUL]:365: "Accesses to non-existent addresses."; [RG]:673: "Accesses to unmapped target
addresses that can be fully represented with the internally used address bits typically return
an error."
|spec

|[[req_bus_11]]`REQ_BUS_11`
|A write answered with an error for any reason other than a failed integrity check shall change
no register.
|[CIP]:214-217: the TileLink error cases "will trigger d_error and won't change the CSR/memory
value."; [RG]:688-689: refusing narrow writes makes it "hard to use a fault injection to cause
only part of a register to be updated"
|spec
|===

The register rows (`REQ_REG_01a`, `REQ_REG_01b`) and the error rows (`REQ_BUS_10a` to
`REQ_BUS_10e`, `REQ_BUS_11`) may be closed by csr_fpv's register-block checker;
they stay rows here. A failed write changing no register is `REQ_BUS_04`.

Questions on these rows: the integrity code, a failed check, a read's data code, an unaligned
address and one response per request (reading RD12),
the alert's causes, delays and test write (reading RD13), an unlisted EG2 index (reading RD32).

[[rq_wakeup]]
== Wakeup detectors

[[req_wakeup_detectors]]
=== Wakeup detectors

*Scope:* `w` is a detector (0 to 7); a cycle is a `clk_aon_i` cycle (watched signal, forwarded
value: xref:{rqm}#terms[terms]).

* Register values are those the AON logic holds once a write has crossed (reading RD18).
* The rows hold with scan mode not True (assumption A1).
* They hold with the mode unchanged while enabled (assumption A5); the other fields may change
  while enabled (reading RD20).
* They hold whatever `sleep_en_i` does (reading RD17).
* They hold whatever `clk_i` does, stopped included: in sleep "only the wakeup detector logic will
  be actively clocked" ([ToO]:39-40).
* They are checked from the filter's fourth sample after `rst_aon_ni` (reading RD46).
* The timed rows (`REQ_WKUP_09a` to `REQ_WKUP_10b`) hold for `CNT_TH` 1 and above: no spec says
  what a timed detector does with 0, the reset value.

[[rq_usb_wakeup]]
== USB wakeup wiring

[[req_usb_wakeup]]
=== USB wakeup

*Scope:* the module is usbdev's AON/Wake module, placed in the pinmux as usbdev is not in the AON
power domain ([ToO]:46-47); what it does is usbdev's spec and testbench (`REQ_USB_06`), and the
other rows check how it is connected. A pinmux port and a port of the module have the same role
when usbdev's docs give the module's port the job of the port the top connects to the pinmux port:

[cols="3,3,5",options="header"]
|===
|Pinmux port |Other end ([TOP] `top_earlgrey.hjson`) |Role ([USB])

|`usbdev_dppullup_en` |usbdev `usb_dp_pullup` (:1337) |D+ pull-up enable, routed to the module's
input `usbdev_dppullup_en_i` (`theory_of_operation.md`:243)
|`usbdev_dnpullup_en` |usbdev `usb_dn_pullup` (:1338) |D- pull-up enable, routed to the module's
input `usbdev_dnpullup_en_i` (:243)
|`usbdev_suspend_req` |usbdev `usb_aon_suspend_req` (:1339) |"Request to activate the AON/Wake
module" (`interfaces.md`:31)
|`usbdev_wake_ack` |usbdev `usb_aon_wake_ack` (:1340) |"Acknowledge a wake signal from the
AON/Wake" (`interfaces.md`:32)
|`usb_dppullup_en` |the top's port `usb_dp_pullup_en` (:1573), to the USB PHY ([IF]:33) |D+
pull-up enable from the module's output `usb_dppullup_en_o` (`theory_of_operation.md`:243)
|`usb_dnpullup_en` |the top's port `usb_dn_pullup_en` (:1574), to the USB PHY ([IF]:34) |D-
pull-up enable from the module's output `usb_dnpullup_en_o` (:243)
|`usbdev_bus_not_idle` |usbdev `usb_aon_bus_not_idle` (:1341) |The event "the USB is in a

(`interfaces.md`:33)
|`usbdev_sense_lost` |usbdev `usb_aon_sense_lost` (:1343) |The event "the VBUS/SENSE signal became

|===
|ID |Requirement |Source |Kind

|[[req_dbg_01a]]`REQ_DBG_01a`
|At each `strap_en_i` pulse, the latch shall take On if `lc_hw_debug_en_i` is On.
|[ToO]:154; [IF]:21
|spec; timing: DV reading, RD23

|[[req_dbg_01b]]`REQ_DBG_01b`
|At each `strap_en_i` pulse, the latch shall take Off if `lc_hw_debug_en_i` is not On.
|[ToO]:154; [IF]:21
|spec; timing: DV reading, RD23

|[[req_dbg_02]]`REQ_DBG_02`
|With no `strap_en_i` pulse, no clear and no full reset, the latch shall keep its value, through
an NDM reset too.
|[ToO]:151-155; rv_dm `doc/interfaces.md`:77-80
|spec; which reset: DV reading, RD24; the NDM reset half is not covered by formal: reset behaviour out of scope

|[[req_dbg_03]]`REQ_DBG_03`
|`lc_hw_debug_clr_i` at any value other than Off shall turn the latch Off.
|[ToO]:158: "The TAP selection logic also clears the sampled `lc_hw_debug_en` whenever any of
`lc_check_byp_en`, `lc_escalate_en` or `lc_hw_debug_clr` is not Off."; [LC] `lc_ctrl.hjson`:358:
"Flops storing the value of `lc_hw_debug_en` (see below) must be cleared whenever this signal is
not Off.", :372; [LC] `theory_of_operation.md`:160: "A module must clear the flop whenever
HW_DEBUG_CLR is not OFF."
|spec

|[[req_dbg_04]]`REQ_DBG_04`
|`lc_check_byp_en_i` at any value other than Off shall turn the latch Off.
|[ToO]:158: "The TAP selection logic also clears the sampled `lc_hw_debug_en` whenever any of
`lc_check_byp_en`, `lc_escalate_en` or `lc_hw_debug_clr` is not Off."; [ToO]:159; [IF]:20
|spec

|[[req_dbg_05]]`REQ_DBG_05`
|`lc_escalate_en_i` at any value other than Off shall turn the latch Off.
|[ToO]:158; [LC] `interfaces.md`:172
|spec

|[[req_dbg_06]]`REQ_DBG_06`
|`lc_hw_debug_clr_i` and `lc_check_byp_en_i` at Off shall not turn the latch Off.
|[ToO]:152: "the `lc_hw_debug_en` state needs to be memorized"; [ToO]:158
|spec

|[[req_dbg_07a]]`REQ_DBG_07a`
|`pinmux_hw_debug_en_o` shall be On while the latch is On.
|[IF]:21; [REG] hjson:416-421
|spec

|[[req_dbg_07b]]`REQ_DBG_07b`
|`pinmux_hw_debug_en_o` shall be Off while the latch is not On.
|[IF]:21; [REG] hjson:416-421
|spec

|[[req_dbg_08]]`REQ_DBG_08`
|After a full reset, the latch shall be Off until the next `strap_en_i` pulse.
|[IF]:21: "This is the latched version of lc_hw_debug_en_i"; [LC]
`lc_ctrl.hjson`:370: "This signal is Off while lc_ctrl is in reset."
|DV reading, RD24

|[[req_dbg_09]]`REQ_DBG_09`
|A clear in the cycle of a `strap_en_i` pulse shall leave the latch Off.
|[ToO]:160
|DV reading, RD26
|===

The On and Off values of these rows: the life cycle enable encoding differs between the [LC] text
and the life cycle package. The clear on any value other than Off
(`REQ_DBG_03`, `REQ_DBG_04`) follows the clear inputs' own texts against [LC]'s generic rule that a
value other than On reads as Off.

Questions on these rows: the reset trees and the reset value (reading RD24), a clear at the pulse
(reading RD26), timing (reading RD23).

'''

[[req_tap_selection]]
=== TAP selection and the JTAG pads

*Scope:* the JTAG pads are IOR3 TCK, IOR0 TMS, IOR2 TDI, IOR4 TRST_N, IOR1 TDO (MIO 38, 35, 37,
39, 36; [TOP] `top_earlgrey.hjson`:1895-1899). The rows hold once the straps and life cycle
inputs have held for the delay of reading RD23; in scan mode a connected TAP's TRST_N is `rst_ni`
(`REQ_TAP_13`). A connected TAP: xref:{rqm}#terms[terms].

[cols="2,6,5,3",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Requirement |Source |Kind

|[[req_tap_01a]]`REQ_TAP_01a`
|With TAP straps 01, `lc_jtag_o` shall carry TCK from its pad, in every life cycle state.
|[ToO]:135; [TP] LcJtagWoScanmode_A
|spec; timing: DV reading, RD23

|[[req_tap_01b]]`REQ_TAP_01b`
|With TAP straps 01, `lc_jtag_o` shall carry TMS from its pad, in every life cycle state.
|[ToO]:135; [TP] LcJtagWoScanmode_A
|spec; timing: DV reading, RD23

|[[req_tap_01c]]`REQ_TAP_01c`
|With TAP straps 01, `lc_jtag_o` shall carry TDI from its pad, in every life cycle state.
|[ToO]:135; [TP] LcJtagWoScanmode_A
|spec; timing: DV reading, RD23

|[[req_tap_01d]]`REQ_TAP_01d`
|With TAP straps 01, `lc_jtag_o` shall carry TRST_N from its pad, in every life cycle state.
|[ToO]:135; [TP] LcJtagWoScanmode_A
|spec; timing: DV reading, RD23

|[[req_tap_02a]]`REQ_TAP_02a`
|With TAP straps 10, `rv_jtag_o` shall carry the four input pads while the latch is On.
|[ToO]:136, 152-154; [IF]:21; [TP] RvJtagWoScanmode_A
|spec; timing: DV reading, RD23; the live gating: DV reading,
RD27

|[[req_tap_02b]]`REQ_TAP_02b`
|With TAP straps 10, `rv_jtag_o` shall not carry the four input pads while the latch is Off.
|[ToO]:136, 152-154; [IF]:21; [TP] RvJtagWoScanmode_A
|spec; timing: DV reading, RD23; the live gating: DV reading,
RD27

|[[req_tap_03a]]`REQ_TAP_03a`
|With TAP straps 11, `dft_jtag_o` shall carry the four input pads while `lc_dft_en_i` is On.
|[ToO]:137,
157; [REG] hjson:423-427; [TP] DftJtagWoScanmode_A
|spec; timing: DV reading, RD23

|[[req_tap_03b]]`REQ_TAP_03b`
|With TAP straps 11, `dft_jtag_o` shall not carry the four input pads while `lc_dft_en_i` is Off.
|[ToO]:137,
157; [REG] hjson:423-427; [TP] DftJtagWoScanmode_A
|spec; timing: DV reading, RD23

|[[req_tap_04]]`REQ_TAP_04`
|Every TAP not connected shall receive an all-zero request.
|[ToO]:129; [TP] LcJtagODefault_A, RvJtagODefault_A, DftJtagODefault_A
|spec; timing: DV reading, RD23

|[[req_tap_05]]`REQ_TAP_05`
|`lc_dft_en_i` and `lc_hw_debug_en_i` shall count as On only at 4'b1010, in strap sampling, the
latch and TAP selection.
|[LC] `interfaces.md`:170-171; [REG] hjson:401-408
|spec

|[[req_tap_06a]]`REQ_TAP_06a`
|While a TAP is connected, pad IOR1 shall drive the TAP's TDO.
|[TP] LcJtagI_A, RvJtagI_A, DftJtagI_A
|spec; which pad: DV reading, RD28; in sleep: waits on
gap

|[[req_tap_06b]]`REQ_TAP_06b`
|While a TAP is connected, pad IOR1 shall drive the TAP's output enable.
|[TP] LcJtagI_A, RvJtagI_A, DftJtagI_A
|spec; which pad: DV reading, RD28; in sleep: waits on
gap

|[[req_tap_07]]`REQ_TAP_07`
|While a TAP is connected, pads IOR0, IOR2, IOR3 and IOR4 shall have output enable 0.
|[ToO]:129-145: silent; the TAPs' standard JTAG port takes TCK, TMS, TRST_N and TDI as pad inputs
and drives only TDO and its enable ([RVDM] `interfaces.md`:84, 89-94; [LC] `interfaces.md`:106-107)
|DV reading, RD28; in sleep: gap

|[[req_tap_08]]`REQ_TAP_08`
|While a TAP is connected, every attribute of the five JTAG pads shall be 0.
|[ToO]:144-145; [TP] MioJtagAttrO_A differs
|spec; "while the JTAG is enabled": DV reading, RD28

|[[req_tap_09]]`REQ_TAP_09`
|Connecting a TAP shall not change the JTAG pads' attribute registers.
|[ToO]:144: "this does not affect the values in the CSRs"
|spec; "while the JTAG is enabled": DV reading, RD28

|[[req_tap_10]]`REQ_TAP_10`
|While a TAP is connected, a peripheral input that selects a JTAG pad shall read 0 or the pad.
|[TP] InSelN_A, MioToPeriph0Backward_A
|spec; out of scope: DV reading, RD43

|[[req_tap_11]]`REQ_TAP_11`
|While a TAP is connected and a JTAG pad's sleep mode is active, the pad shall carry one of two
candidate outcomes, not yet decided: the TAP's signals, as [TP]'s JTAG rows want, or its sleep
value, as [TP]'s sleep rows want.
|[TP] LcJtagI_A, RvJtagI_A, DftJtagI_A (TP:751-769): "When Lc tap is selected, the
corresponding `mio_out_o` and `mio_out_oe` should be equal to `lc_jtag_i`.", with no sleep case;
[TP] MioSleepMode0_A to MioSleepMode3_A (TP:203-290) name no JTAG case
|spec; gap; no side taken: DV reading,
RD44

|[[req_tap_12]]`REQ_TAP_12`
|An NDM reset with no clear shall leave a connected RISC-V TAP connected.
|[RVDM] `interfaces.md`:77-80; [ToO]:151-152; [LC] `lc_ctrl.hjson`:371: "In order to prevent a
JTAG disconnect during non-debug-module (NDM) reset, this signal should be flopped outside the
NDM reset domain."
|spec; which reset: DV reading, RD24; the live gating: DV reading,
RD27; not covered by formal: reset behaviour out of scope

|[[req_tap_13]]`REQ_TAP_13`
|In scan mode, a connected TAP's TRST_N shall be `rst_ni`.
|[TP] LcJtagWScanmode_A, RvJtagWScanmode_A, DftJtagWScanmode_A
|spec
|===

The rule on a peripheral input that selects a JTAG pad (`REQ_TAP_10`) is out of scope: either
value meets the spec (reading RD43).

Questions on these rows: what a peripheral reads (reading RD43), sleep against a TAP (reading
RD44), timing (reading RD23), the pads' roles (reading RD28), the live gating (reading RD27), the
reset trees (reading RD24).

'''

[[req_dft_straps]]
=== DFT straps

*Scope:* `dft_strap_test_o` holds a valid bit and the straps, bit 0 from IOR5 (MIO 40) and bit 1
from IOR7 (MIO 42) ([TP] DftStrapTestO_A; [TOP] `top_earlgrey.hjson`:1892-1893).

[cols="2,6,5,3",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Requirement |Source |Kind

|[[req_dft_01a]]`REQ_DFT_01a`
|At a `strap_en_i` pulse with `lc_dft_en_i` On, `dft_strap_test_o` shall take valid 1.
|[ToO]:112-113,
121, 125; [IF]:25; [TP] DftStrapTestO_A
|spec; the states as signals: DV reading, RD22; the sampled cycle: DV reading,
RD49

|[[req_dft_01b]]`REQ_DFT_01b`
|At a `strap_en_i` pulse with `lc_dft_en_i` On, the straps of `dft_strap_test_o` shall take the
DFT strap pads' values.
|[ToO]:112-113,
121, 125; [IF]:25; [TP] DftStrapTestO_A
|spec; the states as signals: DV reading, RD22; the sampled cycle: DV reading,
RD49

|[[req_dft_02a]]`REQ_DFT_02a`
|Once valid, `dft_strap_test_o` shall keep valid 1 until a full reset.
|[TP] DftStrapTestOValidStable_A, DftStrapTestOStrapStable_A
|spec; which reset: DV reading, RD24

|[[req_dft_02b]]`REQ_DFT_02b`
|Once valid, `dft_strap_test_o` shall keep its straps until a full reset.
|[TP] DftStrapTestOValidStable_A, DftStrapTestOStrapStable_A
|spec; which reset: DV reading, RD24

|[[req_dft_03]]`REQ_DFT_03`
|Before a sample at a `strap_en_i` pulse with `lc_dft_en_i` On, `dft_strap_test_o` shall be all 0,
whatever the DFT strap pads carry.
|[CHIP]:214-215
|spec; never sampled: RTL, RD25
|===

Questions on these rows: the unsampled value (reading RD25), the reset (reading RD24), when the
straps sample (reading RD22), the sampled cycle (reading RD49).

'''
